verdict.summary: Getting your own Slack app working in your own workspace is quick and needs no review. Unlisted public distribution needs a checklist but no review. Marketplace listing is a manual, multi-week review, and Composio's default scope set includes scopes Slack restricts or scrutinises, so you must trim scopes and justify each one.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Gate 1: about 30-60 min (estimate). Gate 2: about 1-2 hours (estimate). Gate 3: several days of documentation, assets and test accounts (estimate).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Minutes to about an hour once you are signed in to api.slack.com/apps (estimate; not timed in research)
verdict.approval_wait: None for own-workspace use or unlisted public distribution (per findings). Marketplace: preliminary check up to 10 business days, then functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions.

gates.name: Own-workspace install (no public distribution)
gates.unlocks: Create the app and connect your own account. The app installs only in the workspace where it was created and gives a single token. Other workspaces need a full OAuth flow.
limits: Until public distribution is enabled, the app can be installed only in its home workspace.
Access tokens do not expire; they are revoked on uninstall, config removal, or deactivation of the authenticating user.
Scopes accumulate per user across authorizations and cannot be removed without revoking the token.

gates.name: Unlisted public distribution (Activate Public Distribution)
gates.unlocks: Enable public distribution from Manage Distribution after completing the checklist. You get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL for invited pilot customers and other workspaces.
limits: Unlisted commercially distributed apps are limited on conversations.history and conversations.replies to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request (new unlisted apps and new installs from 29 May 2025).
Reports say the same limits hit existing unlisted installs from 3 March 2026; Slack's changelog says existing installs are not affected. Unresolved.
Slack says unlisted distribution suits pilots; commercial distribution should go through Marketplace approval.
Workspace admins can restrict installs to admins or Marketplace-listed apps, or require admin approval.
Redirect URLs and other URLs must use SSL.
No install cap for unlisted apps was found.
gates.time_to_reach: Checklist-based; time not stated in findings

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Listing in the Slack Marketplace and commercial distribution through Slack's channel. Public distribution must be enabled before submission.
limits: Needs at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) and testing on a workspace other than your own, including uninstall.
Each scope needs a written justification. Scopes for future features are rejected.
Apps requesting enhanced-review scopes receive an enhanced security review, which Slack may run at any time after submission.
Published apps are locked; scope or redirect changes take effect only after re-review and publishing.
gates.time_to_reach: Preliminary check up to 10 business days, then functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions (6 weeks for resubmitted published apps). Community sources cite 1-2 weeks, which conflicts with Slack's figures; use Slack's.

steps.title: Decide: Composio managed app or your own Slack app
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Slack OAuth app for quick internal or testing use. Register your own Slack app if you need your own client ID and secret, your own redirect URI, or a Marketplace listing. Composio's default scope set is very broad, so do not reuse it for your own app.
gotchas: Composio's default scopes include search:read.*, *:history scopes and files:read, which Slack puts on its enhanced-review list.

steps.title: Sign in and create the app
steps.detail: Open api.slack.com/apps and sign in to your Slack account; the console will not let you create an app without signing in. Create a new app in your own workspace from App Management.
gotchas: Exact menu labels were not captured in research (login required). Check the live page for current labels.

steps.title: Add the Redirect URL
steps.detail: In the app's Redirect URLs setting in App Management, add the callback URL from your Composio auth config. The URL must use HTTPS and must not contain an anchor (#).

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect_uri in the authorize request must match or sit under a configured Redirect URL.
If several redirect URLs are configured, repeat the same redirect_uri at token exchange.

steps.title: Set only the scopes you use
steps.detail: Add bot scopes and user scopes only for features you ship. Mark scopes that users may decline as optional (bot_optional / user_optional in the manifest, or in App Settings). Do not paste Composio's default list.
gotchas: Every scope must be demonstrated, and the app must handle a declined optional scope.
Scopes added later need existing installs to reinstall to receive them.

steps.title: Copy client ID and client secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client ID (shown on the App Management page) and client secret into your Composio custom auth config. Save the config and confirm the authorize and token URLs match the standard install flow.
gotchas: The temporary code expires after ten minutes. Check the state value before exchanging the code.

steps.title: Run a test authorization in your home workspace
steps.detail: Run a test OAuth authorization in your home workspace and confirm the token exchange succeeds. An agent with access can drive this step and report which scopes were granted.
gotchas: Scopes accumulate across authorizations for the same user. Use a clean test user to check a reduced scope set.

steps.title: Test uninstall and reinstall
steps.detail: Uninstall the app and reinstall it to confirm the flow works from a clean state. Note that uninstalling revokes tokens.

steps.title: Enable unlisted public distribution (Gate 2)
steps.detail: Open Manage Distribution, complete the checklist, and select Activate Public Distribution. This gives you an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL for pilot customers. Unlisted distribution is for pilots, not commercial distribution.
gotchas: Public distribution cannot be turned off once enabled (pkce_enabled is app-level; see open questions).

steps.title: Test in a second workspace and check install rules
steps.detail: Install the app in a workspace other than your own and test the full flow, including uninstall. Check whether the target workspace restricts installs to admins or to Marketplace-listed apps, or requires admin approval.
gotchas: The permissions your app requests weigh heavily in admin approval decisions.

steps.title: Check rate limits if you use conversation history
steps.detail: If your unlisted app reads conversation history, test it against the 1-per-minute and 15-object limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Plan for these limits or use a Marketplace listing.
gotchas: Reports conflict on whether existing unlisted installs are affected; test with a current install.

steps.title: Draft listing and review materials
steps.detail: Draft a scope justification for each scope, an app-specific privacy policy covering data collected, use, retention and deletion, a 10-word-or-fewer short description, and an install and uninstall guide. Include an LLM disclosure and accuracy disclaimer if the app exposes an LLM. Do not change the app after review without re-review.
gotchas: Privacy policy must be app-specific, not a generic corporate one (community source).
Slack data may not be used to train LLMs.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and a demo video
steps.detail: Create a distinctive icon that does not resemble Slackbot or the Slack logo, 1600x1000 screenshots (jpg, jpeg or png, under 2MB), and a 30-90 second demo video covering install and OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall. Host the video as a public YouTube link and host the landing page publicly, not behind login.
gotchas: Landing page cannot be a PDF or a repository.

steps.title: Confirm Marketplace prerequisites
steps.detail: Confirm the app is installed on at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days), is fully functional and publicly installable, and has a support channel that does not need a second account, with replies within 2 business days. Apps without customers or built for internal use are not suitable.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Enable public distribution, then open Submit to the Slack Marketplace in app configuration (see the Manage Distribution review checklist). Automated checks run first. Provide test accounts for any third-party service the app connects to. Do not provide Slack workspace credentials.
gotchas: Each resubmission in the preliminary stage resets queue position.
Scopes in Composio's default list (search:read.*, *:history, files:read) add enhanced security review; trim them unless you need them.

steps.title: Wait for preliminary and functional review
steps.detail: Slack checks listing, documentation and scope reasons first (up to 10 business days), then runs a functional review (up to 10 weeks for new submissions). A security review may follow; Slack may ask follow-up questions and does not announce test timing.
gotchas: Security review correspondence comes from a Salesforce-domain address (slack-marketplace-security@salesforce.com). Watch that address.
Have a feature-complete app, a sample use case with click paths, a security contact email and phone, and a test login per permission role with test data ready.

steps.title: Maintain after approval
steps.detail: Keep at least one collaborator on the app. Any substantial change to features or purpose requires resubmission. Scope or redirect URL changes take effect only after re-review and publishing.
gotchas: Slack may run an advanced security review at any time; apps must use TLS 1.2 or later.

requirements.item: Sign-in to Slack to create the app
requirements.detail: The app console requires a Slack account sign-in before you can create an app.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URL with no anchor
requirements.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS and cannot contain an anchor; redirect_uri must match a configured URL.
Each scope needs a written justification; scopes for future features are rejected.
Legacy/restricted scopes, admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute and triggers:* are excluded from Marketplace listing.
search:read.*, *:history, files:read, canvases:read and certain write scopes trigger an enhanced security review.
At least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) and tested on a non-developer workspace, including uninstall.
30-90 second demo covering install and OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall; hosted as a public YouTube link.

requirements.item: Public landing page, privacy policy and support channel
requirements.detail: Landing page not behind login; app-specific privacy policy covering collection, use, retention and deletion with a contact; support channel without a second account, 2-business-day response.
Short description of 10 words or fewer; distinctive icon not resembling Slackbot or Slack; 1600x1000 screenshots under 2MB; pricing model selected.
Apps must delete a user's data within 14 business days after deletion or discontinuation.
All traffic must use TLS 1.2 or later.
If the app exposes an LLM: disclose model and data retention/residency, add accuracy disclaimer, and do not train LLMs on Slack data.
Export Control Classification Number of EAR99 or 5D992 (mass market); you classify the app under the EAR.
Apps distributed beyond their home workspace need SSL on OAuth redirect, interaction, options-load and Events API request URLs.
Apps may not expose private channel names or messages to people who lack access in Slack.

requirements.item: Publicly accessible privacy policy and install instructions
requirements.detail: Developer policy requires a public privacy policy, a link to installation instructions and a customer support contact.

scopes.scope: search:read.files, search:read.im, search:read.mpim, search:read.private, search:read.public, search:read.users
scopes.effect: On Slack's enhanced security review list. Adds security review on submission and needs a clear use case. Drop unless the app searches Slack content.
Excluded from Marketplace listing by Slack's guidelines. Composio's default set includes it.

Broad message access. Slack says it is unlikely to be approved without a use case such as Real-time Search or an MCP server. Enhanced review applies. Community sources say reviewers scrutinise these more closely.
On Slack's enhanced security review list. Community sources say reviewers scrutinise it more closely.
Findings list user groups:write and mpim:write on the enhanced-review list. Confirm whether your use is user-token or bot-token before submitting.

scopes.scope: All other default scopes (for example chat:write, channels:read, files:write, reactions:write, reminders:write, team:read)
scopes.effect: Tier not stated in findings. Each still needs a written justification and must be tied to a feature you can test. Request only what you ship.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission rejected or sent to enhanced security review because of scopes
blockers.cause: Composio's default scope set includes search:read.*, *:history, files:read and search:read, which Slack excludes or scrutinises.
blockers.fix: Build your own Slack app, request only the scopes you ship, and justify each one in writing.

blockers.symptom: Unlisted app hits rate limit on conversations.history or conversations.replies (1 request per minute, 15 objects)
blockers.cause: Slack's May 2025 change for new unlisted commercially distributed apps and new installs; community reports say existing installs were hit in March 2026.
blockers.fix: Keep history access to a minimum, plan around the limit, or move commercial distribution to a Marketplace listing. Confirm the current status of existing installs.

blockers.symptom: App not accepted for the Marketplace (internal-only, unfinished, or no customers)
blockers.cause: Slack says apps built for internal team use, fun, unfinished apps, or apps without customers are unsuitable.
blockers.fix: Only submit once the app is fully functional and tested with other customers. Otherwise use own-workspace or unlisted distribution.

blockers.symptom: Update to scopes or redirect URLs not effective, or existing installs lack new scopes
blockers.cause: Scope changes need existing installs to reinstall. Published app config is locked and changes need re-review.
blockers.fix: Plan scope changes ahead of submission. After publishing, expect re-review and ask existing users to reinstall.

blockers.symptom: Install blocked in a customer workspace
blockers.cause: The workspace admin restricts installs to admins or Marketplace-listed apps, or requires admin approval, and weighs the requested permissions heavily.
blockers.fix: Request minimal scopes and list the app on the Marketplace, or ask the customer admin to approve the install.

composio.note: Use Composio's managed Slack app for quick internal or testing use. Its default scope set is very broad and includes scopes Slack restricts or puts on enhanced review (search:read.*, *:history, files:read, and search:read, which Slack excludes from Marketplace listing). Register your own Slack app at api.slack.com/apps if you need your own client ID and secret, your own redirect URI, or a Marketplace listing, and request only the scopes you use. Whether Composio's managed app can be used for a Marketplace listing was not determined.

evidence.claim: The Slack app console at api.slack.com/apps requires a Slack sign-in to create an application.
evidence.quote: You'll need to sign in to your Slack account to create an application.

evidence.claim: The standard install flow sends users to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with the app's client ID and a scope list; user scopes use a separate user_scope parameter.
After approval Slack returns a temporary code that expires after ten minutes; the app checks state and exchanges the code at oauth.v2.access with client_id and client_secret.
Redirect URLs must use HTTPS and cannot contain an anchor; redirect_uri must match or sit under a configured Redirect URL and must repeat at token exchange when several are configured.
OAuth access tokens do not expire; they are revoked on uninstall, config removal, or deactivation of the authenticating user. Refresh-token rotation is opt-in for granular permissions apps.
Scopes accumulate across repeated authorizations for the same user and cannot be removed from an existing token without revoking it.
Optional scopes can be marked via App Settings or the manifest's bot_optional and user_optional fields; apps must demonstrate every scope and handle declined optional scopes.

Marketplace guidelines exclude apps using legacy or restricted scopes, broad workspace data scopes without clear use, or scopes such as admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute and triggers:*.

Broad message and file access (user *:history scopes) is unlikely to be approved without a use case such as Real-time Search or an MCP server; admin.* is unlikely for apps outside the partner program.
Apps requesting enhanced-review scopes (search:read.*, *:history, files:read, canvases:read, user groups:write/mpim:write, conversations.connect:write) receive an enhanced security review.
Each scope needs a written justification; Slack approves only scopes tied to testable functionality and rejects scopes for future features.
A Marketplace submission needs the app installed on at least 10 active workspaces (used in the past 28 days) and tested there.

evidence.claim: Unlisted commercially distributed apps are limited on conversations.history and conversations.replies to 1 request per minute and 15 objects per request, for new unlisted apps and new installs from 29 May 2025; Marketplace and internal customer-built apps are excluded.
Community reports say the same limits hit existing unlisted installs on 3 March 2026, while Slack's changelog says existing installs are not impacted; unresolved.
Slack's API terms say the Marketplace is the appropriate channel for commercial distribution; unlisted apps are for development and testing.
Marketplace submission requires public distribution to be enabled first; the review checklist is on the Manage Distribution page under Submit to the Slack App Directory.
Slack's directory docs describe a manual review by the App Directory team, with an interactive checklist highlighting missing or insufficient items.
A third-party listing site cites a one-to-two-week review, which conflicts with Slack's published 10-business-day and 10-week timelines; use Slack's figures.
A community guide says reviewers reject apps without an app-specific privacy policy and scrutinise sensitive scopes such as channels:history or files:read.
Slack says apps built for fun or internal team use, unfinished apps, apps without customers, and apps enabling financial transactions or NFT transfers are unsuitable for the App Directory.
Slack's privacy model bars apps from exposing private channel names or messages to people who would not already have access in Slack.

Slack's Security Review may run on published Marketplace apps; reviewers may scan web apps and networks, verify least-privilege scopes, test for vulnerabilities, and review architecture, and may ask follow-up questions.

For security review, provide a feature-complete app, a sample use case with click paths, a security contact email and phone, and a test login for each permission role with populated test data; an architecture diagram is optional.
The security review is not a certification; testing timing is not announced; correspondence comes from slack-marketplace-security@salesforce.com.

Unlisted public distribution is enabled from Manage Distribution after completing the checklist via Activate Public Distribution, yielding an Add to Slack button and shareable install URL; suits pilots, while commercial distribution goes through Marketplace approval.
Until public distribution is enabled, an app can be installed only in its home workspace and gives a single token; other workspaces require an OAuth flow.
Apps distributed beyond their home workspace must support SSL on OAuth redirect URLs, interaction request URLs, options-load URLs and Events API request URLs.
Workspaces can restrict installs to admins or Marketplace-listed apps, or enable admin approval; requested permissions weigh heavily in those decisions.
Changing manifest scopes requires existing installs to reinstall; apps.manifest.update flags permissions_updated, which also fires for redirect URL, PKCE and token management changes.

The App Developer Policy requires deletion of a user's data within 14 business days after deletion or discontinuation, bars LLM training on Slack data, bars unneeded scopes, and requires a public privacy policy.

The App Developer Policy requires a distinctive icon not resembling Slackbot or the Slack icon, bars changing look, function or disclosures without re-review, and requires a link to installation instructions and customer support contact.
The App Developer Policy requires an Export Control Classification Number of EAR99 or 5D992 (mass market), and developers must classify their own apps under the EAR.

open_questions: Exact App Management field labels for Redirect URLs and client ID/secret were not captured (login required). Check the live console.
Developer program prerequisites (free account, partner program, business verification, org admin) were not confirmed beyond the sign-in wall.
No install cap for unlisted or unreviewed apps was found. Whether Activate Public Distribution involves any review was not stated in the findings.
Changelog entries from 2025/07/08 ('Installation requirement for Slack Marketplace apps') and 2026/09/01 ('Updated installation requirement') were not read and may change install gating.

PKCE: a changelog says it became generally available on 2026-03-30 but was not read. Whether PKCE applies to all app types is unconfirmed. Distribution docs say pkce_enabled is app-level and cannot be turned off once on.
Conflict on whether the 2025 conversations.history limits now apply to existing unlisted installs.
Whether Composio's managed Slack app can be used for a Marketplace listing was not determined; Composio's default scopes include scopes Slack restricts.
Security-review fees, minimum timelines for enhanced security reviews, and any limit on submissions were not found.
Rejection patterns beyond Slack's guidelines come only from community sources and were not checked against actual Slack review outcomes.
Timeline conflict: a third-party site cites 1-2 weeks for review; Slack publishes 10 business days (preliminary) and up to 10 weeks (functional). This guide uses Slack's figures.
